title: One Player Template, Many Separate Players
key_insight: When a game needs 100 similar players with separate health, one class can hold the shared rules while each object keeps its own data.
body:
## One Cutter, Many Cookies

You need 100 game players with the same abilities but different names and health. A class is the reusable cutter; each player object is a separate cookie made from it.

The setup method fills in a new object's starting data. Inside a method, self simply means “this particular object,” so damaging Mina does not damage Leo.

Models use classes for the same reason: each model keeps its own learned numbers beside the actions that use them.
common_mistakes: Thinking the class is one of the players — the class is the blueprint; `mina` and `leo` are objects made from it.
Leaving `self` out of a method — Python needs it to know which object's data the method should use.
Expecting one object's change to affect every object — values stored on `self` belong to that one object.
mini_exercise: Add a `heal(amount)` method that increases one player's health. Create two players, heal only one, and print both health values.
real_world_usage: PyTorch models inherit from `nn.Module`. A model object keeps layers and learned parameters together and provides a `forward` method that describes how input data moves through them.
explain_back_prompt: Explain the difference between a class and an object using the two-player example. What does `self` point to?
